your_life.name: Inspector Arun Mehra
your_life.recollections:
The district coat still carries the smell of the coach. Before the uniform there was Mill Lane: your father's wheel plane, your mother's account book, and Tara asking you to wait at the chapel turn. Twelve winters after her death, the institutional letter remains in your desk. You remember its careful wording.

You remember Brin patching the workshop roof after a storm, and Elin copying a difficult account for your mother. Neri repaired a coach wheel on the journey when you first left the valley. These memories concern ordinary help given years ago.

You came back to Bhairav's Hollow on ordinary leave. The road is under snow, the lamps are lit, and people are still finishing the day's work.

now.immediately_visible: Vesper Rane, Joel Arden lies motionless here.

place.name: Old bridge crossing
place.description: The old bridge crosses a narrow channel between the firs. A path climbs back to the boarding yard. The river can be heard beneath its ice. The bridge approach, the bank and anything below the crossing can be inspected separately. The coach lies below the bridge, its near wheel folded under the axle. Snow softens the outlines of the wreckage and broken timbers. Vesper Rane, Joel Arden lie motionless here.

task.name: The Second Passenger
task.scope: Investigate two deaths at the bridge crossing. Establish responsibility for the deaths and whether either passenger was specifically targeted. Distinguish an observed act, the failure mechanism and evidence of intention.
task.success: Support both death attributions and the intended-target finding using acquired evidence, with no false or unsupported conclusions.
task.briefing: The coach lies below the old bridge. Two people who expected a short journey have died, and news is travelling faster than anyone has checked it. You arrive at the crossing as the district investigator. Begin with the scene, then follow the route back through the town. What the passengers intended, what other people witnessed and what happened to the coach must be established through the investigation.

findings.label: body of Vesper Rane
findings.description: The passenger is unresponsive below the broken coach. The injuries are consistent with the fall, not an earlier assault.

findings.label: brake rod
findings.description: The retaining section has a fresh deliberate cut concealed beneath its housing. The rod can no longer hold the brake pawl.

place.name: Coach boarding yard
place.description: A covered bay keeps the worst weather off the coaches. A repair stand faces the gate and a narrow notice board holds the day's departures. The road descends to the bridge; doors lead to the inn, while a short lane reaches the square. From the stand a person can see the rear brake assembly without seeing inside the coach.

people.name: Neri Bell
people.appearance: A repairer wipes grease from a thumb before touching his notebook.

findings.label: inspection card
findings.description: Signed before departure by Neri Bell: the brake-release rod and retaining pawl were intact and held under load. A diagram records their fitted positions.

observation.observation: The fresh cut passes through the retaining section shown intact on the pre-departure inspection card. With that section severed the pawl cannot hold under load. The damage is a disabling cut, not ordinary wear; this identifies a failure mechanism, not the person who caused it.

recollections.text: I inspected the brake before departure. The dated inspection card is on the repair stand.
Brin Calder arrives from Pine Lantern booking room.
Brin Calder cuts the retaining section of the coach brake rod, then sets the housing back over it.
The two passengers board and the coach leaves toward the bridge.

place.name: Pine Lantern booking room
place.description: The booking room smells of damp tickets and tea. A desk holds the dispatch ledger; a writing shelf has been cleared for visitors. The boarding yard is just outside. Passengers have left scarves over the backs of chairs, expecting to return for them after the short journey.

findings.label: dispatch ledger
findings.description: The departure list records Vesper Rane carrying BLUE-17 and Joel Arden carrying AMBER-4 on the same coach. The entries were countersigned before departure.

findings.label: signed business receipt
findings.description: A routine business receipt is signed in full by Brin Calder. The hand has a distinctive joined final r.

findings.label: route instruction
findings.description: A folded instruction reads: “The packet marked BLUE-17 must not reach the regional office. Disable the downhill brake on its coach.” The lower corner carries initials, not a full signature. Its close lettering has a joined final r.

place.description: A covered bay keeps the worst weather off the coaches. A repair stand faces the gate and a narrow notice board holds the day's departures. The road descends to the bridge; doors lead to the inn, while a short lane reaches the square. From the stand a person can see the rear brake assembly without seeing inside the coach.

place.name: Toll office at the square
place.description: The toll office has a broad public counter and a low stove. Receipts are tied in monthly bundles, with specimen signatures in the cover book. The boarding yard lies along the lane. A clerk has left enough lamp oil for the last accounts to be checked.

findings.label: signed business receipt
findings.description: A routine business receipt is signed in full by Elin Frost. Its hand is evenly spaced and upright.

observation.observation: The dispatch code in the instruction resolves in the countersigned departure ledger to Vesper Rane. The other passenger has a different dispatch code. This identifies the addressed packet, not the note’s author. The lettering in the route instruction agrees with the independently signed business receipt, including the joined final r.
